# CLI safety: export/import help text warnings

## Context
After a destructive `wl import` incident in the SorraAgents project (a work item was moved between projects via export/import and the source DB was replaced), the operator requested (2026-08-27, Tableau-Card-Engine session herdr-1787866878):

> make the --help text for import and export much clearer. Warn that export will export the entire database and import will replace the entire database

## Change
- `src/commands/export.ts`: description now warns the export writes the entire database (all items, comments, dependency edges) to the JSONL file.
- `src/commands/import.ts`: description now warns import is destructive — it REPLACEs the entire database with only the items in the JSONL file.

Both are description-only changes to the CLI help; no behavior change.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. `wl export --help` output contains the warning that export writes the entire database.
2. `wl import --help` output contains the warning that import is destructive and REPLACEs the entire database.
3. Existing test suite passes (the changes are description-only; no CLI behavior changes).
data.title: Warn in wl export/import --help that export dumps the whole DB and import REPLACEs it

# Child 1: Stop re-sort from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` (`packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769`) runs `UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ?` with a single shared `now` for every item whose sortIndex changed. Re-sort runs automatically on `wl next` (unless `--no-re-sort`), on create/update, so routine queue reads rewrite `updatedAt` on dozens of items at once (observed: 13 items at `2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z`, 88 items at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`).

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: audit counts only if `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit. Concrete victim: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V audited "Ready to close: Yes" 2026-09-03 now carries `updatedAt` 2026-09-11, so its passing audit reads stale and the item lingers in the open queue. Recency-weighted scoring (`database.ts:2215-2216`) is also polluted.

## Users

- **Producer/operator:** a "Ready to close: Yes" item must stay ready across mechanical re-sorts.
- **Heartbeat/audit pipeline:** must not re-audit items whose only change is sortIndex.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` (and the `database.ts:755-767` single-item re-sort path) no longer bump `updatedAt` when the only change is `sortIndex`. Semantic edits elsewhere still bump `updatedAt` as today.
- [ ] Regression test: audit an item "Ready to close: Yes", run `reSort`, assert the audit is still fresh (`auditedAt >= updatedAt` holds / freshness check passes) and `updatedAt` is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 behavior preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` + `packages/shared/src/database.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Check sibling: WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` — `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:755-793` — re-sort paths; `:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`; `:2215` — recency scoring
- `src/commands/re-sort.ts`

## Related work

- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (sibling timestamp symptom)
- WL-0MM4OA55D1741ETF, WL-0MOYD0UAC003YJA3, WL-0MNX9XIQD005PUVW (auto re-sort features)
- Victim example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V

# Child 1: Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits via `updatedAt` churn

Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 (mechanism 1).

## Problem statement

`batchUpdateSortIndices` in `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts:747-769` stamps `updatedAt = now` alongside `sortIndex` in a single SQL UPDATE:

```sql
UPDATE workitems SET sortIndex = ?, updatedAt = ? WHERE id = ?
```

This means any re-sort operation (triggered automatically on `wl next` unless `--no-re-sort`) bumps the `updatedAt` of every item whose sortIndex changed. The audit-freshness rule (`isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `database.ts:644`) checks `auditedAt >= updatedAt` — so a re-sort after an audit silently invalidates a previously passing audit.

**Evidence:** 13 items share identical `updatedAt=2026-09-11T07:34:26.956Z` with consecutive sortIndex 300-1500; another 88-item cluster at `2026-09-11T08:33:19.554Z`. WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V's passing audit is stale after re-sort.

## Root cause

Sort index is an organizational/concern, not a semantic change. The `updatedAt` field is used by the audit freshness invariant as a proxy for "when did this item last change semantically". Stamping `updatedAt` during sortIndex-only updates conflates mechanical churn with semantic edits.

## Solution

Remove `updatedAt = ?` from the sortIndex-only UPDATE in `batchUpdateSortIndices`. This is a surgical change to a single SQL statement.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `batchUpdateSortIndices` does NOT update `updatedAt` — sortIndex changes are transparent to audit freshness
- [ ] An item with a passing audit (`readyToClose: true`) retains audit freshness across re-sort operations (auditedAt >= updatedAt still holds)
- [ ] Genuine semantic edits (description, title, status, etc.) still bump `updatedAt` — the freshness invariant works correctly for real changes
- [ ] Existing tests for updatedAt preservation (whitespace-only diffs, CAS claims, etc.) still pass
- [ ] New regression test: audit item → re-sort → verify audit still fresh
- [ ] Full project test suite passes

## Constraints

- Minimal change: only modify the SQL in `batchUpdateSortIndices`
- Do not break the existing updatedAt preservation behavior for genuine edits (the update/import/upsert no-op guards already handle this)
- No schema migration needed
- The `reSort` function in database.ts calls `assignSortIndexValuesForItems` → `batchUpdateSortIndices`; only the SQL statement changes

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/persistent-store.ts` — `batchUpdateSortIndices` (line ~747-769)
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — `reSort`, `isAuditNotReadyFresh`, `assignSortIndexValuesForItems`
- `packages/shared/src/database.test.ts` — existing updatedAt tests

## Parent AC coverage

- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC1:** Re-sort no longer invalidates previously fresh audits — this is the primary fix.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC3:** Queue surfaces distinguish semantic edits from mechanical timestamp churn — fixing updatedAt churn at the source enables this.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC4:** New regression test: audit → re-sort → verify freshness.
- **Parent WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9 AC5:** Full suite passes (all children contribute).

## Related work

- Parent: WL-0MTWU13SU008VLW9
- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (audit freshness rule)
- WL-0MSKZ36MT0089UOS (same-timestamp merge bumps updatedAt — sibling symptom)
- WL-0MSJL00P5004Y0L6 (demotion feature — intent to preserve)
- Example: WL-0MTJ7IEI80055V2V (stale audit after re-sort)

# [downtime] Critical items blocked by a filter are never escalated (critical override is dead code)

Parent: WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2

## Problem statement

The dispatcher once had a *critical-first* tier: `getNextCriticalCandidate()` enumerated open critical items across **all** stages and dispatched the highest-priority one with its stage-appropriate skill (implemented by WL-0MTJDZY5E003D6CO, marked completed).

That tier now lives **only** in the legacy tier chain, which runs **only when the Herdr head is empty**. The current source says so explicitly (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` ~line 1700): the tier is *"dead whenever the Herdr head is non-empty"*. Because mandatory critical/`in_review` items always populate the head, the override **never fires**. This is a silent regression introduced by the Herdr-head migration (WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2).

Consequence: a critical item blocked by **any** filter — stale success marker, producer-review flag, audit-freshness, risk/effort — is treated exactly like an ordinary item and is never escalated. It can sit indefinitely while lower-priority work consumes the window.

## Live evidence (2026-09-18)

All three open critical items across the workspace went undispatched for 30+ hours while the dispatcher reported `noCandidate`:

- `CG-0MU4U38HU000AXU2` — Tableau-Card-Engine (`intake_complete`, blocked by stale `plan` marker)
- `WL-0MU55UDBJ008DJ67` — ContextHub (`plan_complete`, blocked by stale `implement` marker)
- `SA-0MSYPAV1R000SMHK` — SorraAgents (`plan_complete`, blocked by stale `implement` marker)

The stale-marker cause is the sibling item. This item addresses the missing **escalation guarantee** for critical work regardless of cause.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The highest-priority open critical item is escalated/re-dispatched within one idle cycle even when a **non-safety** filter (e.g. stale marker) currently excludes it.
2. Genuine **safety** gates still block escalation: `needsProducerReview === true`, code-freeze/ambiguous, active-audit single-flight, per-process single-flight, and the pre-dispatch CAS claim.
3. No second ranking is introduced: critical items are already mandatory-always in the Herdr head; the fix only guarantees a blocked critical item is not starved by non-critical items occupying the window.
4. Regression tests: (a) a critical item blocked by one non-safety filter is dispatched ahead of lower-priority dispatchable items; (b) a critical item blocked by a safety gate is **not** dispatched.
5. Contract documented in `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (what "critical-first" now means under the Herdr-head contract).
6. `npm run build` and the existing suites pass.

## Key files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchDowntimeWork` / offer computation (re-introduce a live critical pass on the Herdr-head path)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getNextCriticalCandidate` wiring
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — contract
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — regression tests

## Constraints

- Must not resurrect the retired tier ordering as a *ranking*; keep "gates are filters on the Herdr sequence".
- Preserve the three-strike / cooldown and single-flight semantics.
